messages.text:
Hello,

Thanks for the photos. I can see them clearly: the first shows the top of a Mean Well style enclosed power supply with the yellow "Voltage Warning" sticker that says to check the voltage setting before powering on (115V for a 110V supply, 230V for a 220V supply), and that the wrong setting will permanently damage the unit, with the note that the selector switch is under the right side of the power supply. The second photo shows the specification and safety label with the output terminals visible along the bottom edge (-V, +V, earth, N, L). The third shows the same warning sticker plus the yellow bilingual label repeating that the AC input voltage must be selected by the switch before power is applied.

So the answer to what you are looking for: the selector is not on the top face you photographed. It is a small recessed slide switch on the side of the case, toward the right hand end when the AC terminal block is facing you, often half hidden behind a cut-out in the metal. On many of these you need a small flat screwdriver or the tip of a pen to move it, and the voltage printed next to the slider position is the setting that is active. Please check it with the unit completely unplugged, never while it is powered.

Set it to 230V if your wall supply is 220 to 240V (most of Europe, UK, Asia, Australia), and to 115V only if you are on 110 to 120V mains (North America, Japan). If you look along that side and there is genuinely no switch and no cut-out, then your unit is a fixed wide-range or 230V only model, which is normal for some batches, and in that case the sticker simply does not apply to it and you can power it on as is.

One thing worth saying plainly: if the supply has already been powered on at 115V while connected to 230V mains, it will usually be damaged and should not be used again. If that happened, keep it unplugged and send me a short note describing what you saw or heard when it was switched on, and I will take it from there.

If you want a quicker back and forth, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and you can mention @nullhashrate, our hardware lead, who is very active there. Otherwise just reply here with a photo of that right hand side of the case and I will point out the switch for you.

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
